facts.text: Downers Grove was founded in 1832 by Pierce Downer, a farmer who traveled to Illinois from Rutland, New York, but was originally from Vermont.
Downers Grove was named for a lush grove of old‑growth bur oak trees surrounding the village, which stood out from the local savanna landscape.
Both the Lyman and Blodgett homes are of cultural significance, as they were both built by abolitionist families and served as former stops on the Underground Railroad.
The Downers Grove Museum and Historical Society present the Historic Home Program, aiming to preserve the village’s homes and educate the community about research and preservation.
